summary: All 7 plan phases complete. Every ungrounded wall-clock assertion in the three named test files was deleted or converted to a behavioural assertion, 5 vacuous tests were deleted, cap-burn was cut, all slow marks were removed from those files (exactly 1 slow-marked test remains repo-wide), and the -m "not slow" quarantine clause was deleted outright from code/pyproject.toml. Verified by three separate unfiltered pytest invocations with an identical green result set: 2190 collected / 2190 passed / 0 failed / 0 deselected each. The 3 failures the research measured are all fixed and pass 3/3; no out-of-scope failure appeared, so the revert contingency was not triggered.
decisions_made: No budget was re-grounded from measured p95/p99: the research's category (a) was empty, because every measured quantity was the bimodal max_time cap rather than the code's cost. The task description's p95/p99 framing is superseded, not skipped.

5 tests deleted as vacuous or duplicate (2 assertTrue(True) placeholders, 1 copy-paste duplicate, 1 cap-pinned scaling ratio, 1 interrupt test that never sent an interrupt). Accounting reconciles: 2195 - 5 = 2190 collected.

None of the plan's three 'if the property does not hold, delete the test' fallbacks was taken: get_theory identity, Syntax structural comparability, and ModelDefaults.max_time exposure were each probed and verified to hold before the conversion was written.
Two try/except bodies were restructured so converted assertions sit outside the try -- left inside, the test's own except Exception would have swallowed its new assertion.
5 timing assertions retained and each documented in place as a hang guard or (test_serialization_performance) a genuine Z3-free averaged micro-benchmark.
pytest-timeout declared in the dev extra (stated scope addition already flagged in the plan's Phase 5) so the retained @pytest.mark.timeout hang guards are not silently ignored in a clean install.
Both concurrency tests left byte-identical and unmarked, verified programmatically; nothing under oracle/ was touched.

Task 135's Phase 7 is the same pyproject deletion performed here and is now marked COMPLETED by reference in its plan, with its gated Testing & Validation checkbox ticked. Task 135's plan has no unfinished phase; its state.json status was deliberately NOT transitioned from inside this task.
dead_ends: Asserting a relative scaling ratio between two N values (the task description's proposed alternative) was measured and rejected in research: under the cap all ratios are ~1.0 and vacuous, and lifting the cap makes identical input vary 129x in-process, so a ratio compounds two noisy measurements rather than cancelling them. Do not retry it.

A first attempt at unfiltered run 3 was killed at 580s by the harness command timeout at 55% progress. That is a truncation, not a result; it was discarded and the run re-executed detached. Full unfiltered runs take ~6-7 min and must be run detached, not under a 10-min foreground cap.
cross_task_note: Task 135 now has no remaining implementation work and can be closed by the orchestrator or /todo.
